title: T‑Mobile Monitoring and Ready to Respond to Tropical Storm Edouard (Updated 9/2/26)
summary: Update: September 2, 2026T‑Mobile continues to monitor Tropical Depression Edouard, with the greatest concern now focused on significant flooding
body_markdown:
# **Update: September 2, 2026**


T‑Mobile continues to monitor Tropical Depression Edouard, with the greatest concern now focused on significant flooding northwest of Beaumont, Texas. Our thoughts remain with everyone affected as heavy rain and dangerous flash flooding continue in the area.


Our network continues to perform well overall. Our teams are out in the field where conditions allow, deploying portable generators, conducting site assessments and working to address remaining coverage gaps. Many localized network issues are tied to commercial power outages, and many affected areas continue to have overlapping coverage.


We are also tracking retail conditions, including a store closure in Livingston, Texas due to flooding. Community support teams remain on standby and are coordinating with local agencies and response partners to understand emerging needs and help support affected communities where conditions allow.


Customers and communities in affected areas should continue to follow guidance from local officials, avoid flooded roadways and keep devices charged where possible. Customers planning to visit a store should check the[T‑Mobile store locator](https://www.t-mobile.com/stores) for the latest available hours and store information before heading out.


We will continue coordinating our response and provide updates as conditions evolve.


To everyone in the affected areas: please stay safe, stay aware and take care of one another.


###


# **September 1, 2026**


T‑Mobile is closely monitoring Tropical Storm Edouard as it moves across the Texas-Louisiana border region. Current forecasts indicate tropical-storm conditions are affecting portions of the upper Texas coast and southwestern Louisiana, with flash flooding, gusty winds, coastal flooding and possible power outages among the primary concerns.


Our thoughts are with everyone in the path of the storm. We know how important it is to stay connected during moments like this, and our teams are ready to respond if conditions require.


Our preparations include:


- Monitoring storm conditions, network performance and critical infrastructure across areas that may be impacted
- Preparing[backup power resources](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/disaster-definitions) , including generators and fuel support where needed
- Positioning mobile network assets and connectivity solutions so they’re ready to deploy if conditions require
- Using our[SON (Self-Organizing Network)](https://tmobile-newsroom.wistia.com/medias/mo96mmphvr) technology to help the network adapt and optimize performance if impacts occur
- Tracking retail locations in the projected path and preemptively closing select stores to help ensure the safety of our employees and customers
- Engaging with federal, state and local emergency management partners to support situational awareness and help address emerging needs
- Opening lines of communication with customers, public safety agencies and critical infrastructure partners to identify connectivity needs and support requests as conditions evolve


Today, we were glad to have American Red Cross partners at our Business Operations Center at our Bellevue, WA headquarters as our teams monitored storm conditions and continued readiness planning.


Customers and communities in the path of the storm are encouraged to prepare now by charging mobile devices and portable power banks, protecting phones and chargers from water damage, downloading trusted weather and emergency apps, saving important contacts, and following guidance from local officials.


We will continue monitoring Tropical Storm Edouard closely and coordinating our response to support our employees, customers and communities. Most importantly, we encourage everyone in potentially impacted areas to take precautions, stay aware and put safety first.


For more information on T‑Mobile’s preparedness and response capabilities, visit the[Emergency Response hub](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/emergency-response) and follow @TMobileNews on[X](https://x.com/tmobilenews) and[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/tmobilenews/) .
